discovery: Discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian), USA

motivation: In 2005 the SDSS (Eisenstein et al.) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Peacock et al.) teams found the imprint of primordial sound waves in the galaxy distribution: a preferred separation of about 150 Mpc, the same acoustic scale seen in the cosmic microwave background. Eisenstein also laid much of the theoretical groundwork that made the signal both predictable and measurable. This turned the large-scale structure of the universe into a standard ruler calibrated by well-understood linear physics, and it is much less affected by the astrophysical systematics, such as dust and progenitor evolution, that limit supernova standard candles. BAO independently confirmed cosmic acceleration and became the backbone of precision cosmology. Today it underpins BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and Euclid, whose 2024-2025 results hint that dark energy may evolve with time. A new observational tool that changed how we measure the cosmos.
